hindi: अब इसके बाद हम 'आरग्वधीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called "Āragvadhīya".
notes: Prose opening formula, not a verse (the unit is typed as "verse"). athāta = athāto with the visarga of ataḥ dropped before ā. āragvadhīya is a taddhita name formed from the chapter's first word, āragvadha.
lines_deva: अथात आरग्वधीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः
lines_iast: athāta āragvadhīyamadhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, not a verse. sma with āha gives a past sense.
lines_deva: इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः
lines_iast: iti ha smāha bhagavānātreyaḥ

hindi: आरग्वध, एडगज सहित करञ्ज, वासा, गुडूची, मदन, दोनों हरिद्रा; श्र्याह्व, सुराह्व, खदिर और धव, निम्ब, विडङ्ग, करवीरक की छाल;
english: Āragvadha, karañja with eḍagaja, vāsā, guḍūcī, madana, the two haridrās; śryāhva, surāhva, khadira and dhava, nimba, viḍaṅga, the bark of karavīraka;
notes: List continues to unit 5; unit 6 says these are six formulations set out in half-verses: line a = formulation 1, line b = formulation 2. saiḍagajaḥ (sa-eḍagajaḥ) may qualify āragvadhaḥ before it or karañjaḥ after it; word order is kept. The two haridrās are taken as haridrā and dāruharidrā (standard, by commentators). śryāhva 'named after Śrī' = śrīveṣṭaka, pine resin (probable); surāhva 'named after the gods' = devadāru (standard). Identifications: āragvadha = Cassia fistula (standard); eḍagaja = Cassia tora (standard); karañja = Pongamia pinnata (standard); vāsā = Adhatoda vasica (standard); guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); madana = Randia dumetorum (standard); haridrā = Curcuma longa, dāruharidrā = Berberis aristata (standard); devadāru = Cedrus deodara (standard); khadira = Acacia catechu (standard); dhava = Anogeissus latifolia (standard); nimba = Azadirachta indica (standard); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard); karavīraka = Nerium indicum (standard).
lines_deva: आरग्वधः सैडगजः करञ्जो वासा गुडूची मदनं हरिद्रे
श्र्याह्वः सुराह्वः खदिरो धवश्च निम्बो विडङ्गं करवीरकत्वक्
lines_iast: āragvadhaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjo vāsā guḍūcī madanaṃ haridre
śryāhvaḥ surāhvaḥ khadiro dhavaśca nimbo viḍaṅgaṃ karavīrakatvak

hindi: भूर्ज की ग्रन्थि, लशुन, लोमश सहित शिरीष, गुग्गुलु और कृष्णगन्धा; फणिज्झक, वत्सक और सप्तपर्ण, पीलु, कुष्ठ और सुमना के प्रवाल;
english: the knot of bhūrja, laśuna, śirīṣa with lomaśa, guggulu and kṛṣṇagandhā; phaṇijjhaka, vatsaka and saptaparṇa, pīlu, kuṣṭha and the young shoots of sumanas;
notes: Formulations 3 (line a) and 4 (line b). granthiḥ bhaurjaḥ = the knot (node) of bhūrja, birch, Betula utilis (standard). salomaśaḥ may attach to śirīṣa before it or to guggulu after it; lomaśa is disputed (some take it as a form of kāsīsa, others as a plant). pīlūni (neuter plural) probably means pīlu fruits. kuṣṭha here is the drug, not the disease. Identifications: laśuna = garlic, Allium sativum (standard); śirīṣa = Albizia lebbeck (standard); guggulu = Commiphora mukul resin (standard); kṛṣṇagandhā = śobhāñjana, Moringa oleifera (standard, by commentators); phaṇijjhaka = a basil, Ocimum sp. (probable); vatsaka = kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica (standard); saptaparṇa = Alstonia scholaris (standard); pīlu = Salvadora persica (standard); kuṣṭha = Saussurea lappa (standard); sumanas = jātī, Jasminum grandiflorum (probable).
lines_deva: ग्रन्थिश्च भौर्जो लशुनः शिरीषः सलोमशो गुग्गुलुकृष्णगन्धे
फणिज्झको वत्सकसप्तपर्णौ पीलूनि कुष्ठं सुमनःप्रवालाः
lines_iast: granthiśca bhaurjo laśunaḥ śirīṣaḥ salomaśo guggulukṛṣṇagandhe
phaṇijjhako vatsakasaptaparṇau pīlūni kuṣṭhaṃ sumanaḥpravālāḥ

words.gloss: kāśīsa, lodhra, arjuna, musta and sarja

hindi: वचा, हरेणु, त्रिवृता, निकुम्भ, भल्लातक, गैरिक और अञ्जन; मनःशिला और आल, गृहधूम, एला, काशीस, लोध्र, अर्जुन, मुस्त और सर्ज —
english: vacā, hareṇu, trivṛt, nikumbha, bhallātaka, red ochre (gairika) and añjana; manaḥśilā and āla, house soot (gṛhadhūma), elā, kāśīsa, lodhra, arjuna, musta and sarja —
notes: Formulations 5 (line a) and 6 (line b). gṛhadhūma: visarga of gṛhadhūmaḥ dropped before e (regular). kāśīsa is spelled with ś here and kāsīsa in unit 10 (both spellings occur). Identifications: vacā = Acorus calamus (standard); hareṇu = reṇukā, seeds of Vitex agnus-castus (disputed); trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); nikumbha = dantī, Baliospermum montanum (standard); bhallātaka = Semecarpus anacardium (standard); añjana = srotoñjana, stibnite or galena (disputed); manaḥśilā = realgar, āla = haritāla, orpiment (standard); elā = Elettaria cardamomum (standard); kāśīsa = green vitriol, ferrous sulphate (standard); lodhra = Symplocos racemosa (standard); arjuna = Terminalia arjuna (standard); musta = Cyperus rotundus (standard); sarja = Vateria indica (probable).
lines_deva: वचा हरेणुस्त्रिवृता निकुम्भो भल्लातकं गैरिकमञ्जनं च
मनःशिलाले गृहधूम एला काशीसलोध्रार्जुनमुस्तसर्जाः
lines_iast: vacā hareṇustrivṛtā nikumbho bhallātakaṃ gairikamañjanaṃ ca
manaḥśilāle gṛhadhūma elā kāśīsalodhrārjunamustasarjāḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार आधे-आधे रूप में बताए गए ये छह चूर्ण-प्रदेह, गोपित्त पिलाकर फिर से पीसे गए और सर्षप-तैल से युक्त, परम सिद्ध हैं; वैद्य को इनका प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: These six powder-plasters (cūrṇa-pradeha), thus set out in half-forms, soaked in cow's bile and ground again, mixed with mustard oil, are supremely proven; they are to be applied by the physician.
notes: ardharūpaiḥ is taken as 'each in the form of a half-verse': lines 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b give the six formulations. gopittapītāḥ literally 'having drunk cow's bile', i.e. impregnated with it. siddhāḥ could also mean 'prepared'; 'proven' fits param.
lines_deva: इत्यर्धरूपैर्विहिताः षडेते गोपित्तपीताः पुनरेव पिष्टाः
सिद्धाः परं सर्षपतैलयुक्ताश्चूर्णप्रदेहा भिषजा प्रयोज्याः
lines_iast: ityardharūpairvihitāḥ ṣaḍete gopittapītāḥ punareva piṣṭāḥ
siddhāḥ paraṃ sarṣapatailayuktāścūrṇapradehā bhiṣajā prayojyāḥ

hindi: प्रयुक्त किए जाने पर ये मनुष्यों के कृच्छ्र कुष्ठों, नए किलास, सुरेशलुप्त, दद्रु सहित किटिभ, भगन्दर और अर्श, तथा पामा सहित अपची को शीघ्र नष्ट कर देंगे।
english: When applied, they would quickly destroy in men the difficult kuṣṭhas (skin diseases), recent kilāsa, sureśalupta, kiṭibha with dadru, bhagandara and arśas, and apacī with pāmā.
notes: sureśa 'lord of the gods' (Indra): sureśalupta is a synonym of indralupta; the epithet is kept in the translation. Disease equivalents: kuṣṭha = a class of chronic skin diseases including leprosy (standard); kilāsa = leucoderma, vitiligo (standard); indralupta = alopecia (areata) (standard); kiṭibha = a rough scaly skin disease, possibly psoriasis (probable); dadru = ringworm, tinea (standard); bhagandara = fistula-in-ano (standard); arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); apacī = chronic lymphadenitis of the neck, scrofula (probable); pāmā = scabies or eczema (probable). tu is left untranslated as a connective.
lines_deva: कुष्ठानि कृच्छ्राणि नवं किलासं सुरेशलुप्तं किटिभं सदद्रु
भगन्दरार्शांस्यपचीं सपामां हन्युः प्रयुक्तास्त्वचिरान्नराणाम्
lines_iast: kuṣṭhāni kṛcchrāṇi navaṃ kilāsaṃ sureśaluptaṃ kiṭibhaṃ sadadru
bhagandarārśāṃsyapacīṃ sapāmāṃ hanyuḥ prayuktāstvacirānnarāṇām

hindi: कुष्ठ, दोनों हरिद्रा, सुरस, पटोल, निम्ब और अश्वगन्धा, सुरदारु और शिग्रु, सर्षप सहित तुम्बुरु, धान्य और वन्य, तथा चण्डा — इनके समान भाग वाले चूर्ण बनाए;
english: One should make powders, in equal parts, of kuṣṭha, the two haridrās, surasa, paṭola, nimba and aśvagandhā, suradāru and śigru, tumburu, dhānya and vanya with sarṣapa, and caṇḍā;
notes: The sentence continues into unit 9. samāni 'equal' is taken as equal quantities of each drug. sasarṣapam grammatically qualifies the compound tumburudhānyavanyam. Identifications: surasa = tulasī, Ocimum sanctum (standard); paṭola = Trichosanthes dioica (standard); aśvagandhā = Withania somnifera (standard); suradāru = devadāru, Cedrus deodara (standard); śigru = Moringa oleifera (standard); sarṣapa = mustard, Brassica sp. (standard); tumburu = Zanthoxylum alatum (standard); dhānya = coriander, Coriandrum sativum (standard); vanya = kaivarta-mustaka, a sedge (disputed); caṇḍā = coraka, Angelica glauca (disputed).
lines_deva: कुष्ठं हरिद्रे सुरसं पटोलं निम्बाश्वगन्धे सुरदारुशिग्रू
ससर्षपं तुम्बुरुधान्यवन्यं चण्डां च चूर्णानि समानि कुर्यात्
lines_iast: kuṣṭhaṃ haridre surasaṃ paṭolaṃ nimbāśvagandhe suradāruśigrū
sasarṣapaṃ tumburudhānyavanyaṃ caṇḍāṃ ca cūrṇāni samāni kuryāt

hindi: उन तक्र में पिसे चूर्णों से पहले तैल लगे शरीर का उद्वर्तन करने का यत्न करे; उससे इसकी कण्डू, कोठ सहित पिडकाएँ, कुष्ठ और शोफ शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: With these, ground in buttermilk (takra), one should first try to rub (udvartana) the body anointed with oil; by that his itching (kaṇḍū), eruptions (piḍakā) with koṭha, kuṣṭhas and swellings (śopha) subside.
notes: taiḥ refers to the powders of unit 8. tenāsya is read tena + asya ('by that, his'); tena + āsya ('itching of the face') is grammatically possible but less natural. kaṇḍūḥ is nom. sg.; the plural verb vrajanti covers all subjects. koṭha = urticarial rash (probable).
lines_deva: तैस्तक्रपिष्टैः प्रथमं शरीरं तैलाक्तमुद्वर्तयितुं यतेत
तेनास्यकण्डूः पिडकाः सकोठाः कुष्ठानि शोफाश्च शमं व्रजन्ति
lines_iast: taistakrapiṣṭaiḥ prathamaṃ śarīraṃ tailāktamudvartayituṃ yateta
tenāsyakaṇḍūḥ piḍakāḥ sakoṭhāḥ kuṣṭhāni śophāśca śamaṃ vrajanti

words.gloss: kuṣṭha, amṛtāsaṅga, kaṭaṅkaṭerī, kāsīsa, kampillaka, musta and lodhra

hindi: कुष्ठ, अमृतासङ्ग, कटङ्कटेरी, कासीस, कम्पिल्लक, मुस्त और लोध्र; सौगन्धिक, सर्जरस, विडङ्ग, मनःशिला और आल, करवीरक की छाल —
english: Kuṣṭha, amṛtāsaṅga, kaṭaṅkaṭerī, kāsīsa, kampillaka, musta and lodhra; saugandhika, the resin of sarja, viḍaṅga, manaḥśilā and āla, the bark of karavīraka —
notes: List of ingredients; the sentence continues into unit 11. Identifications: amṛtāsaṅga = tuttha, copper sulphate (probable, by commentators); kaṭaṅkaṭerī = dāruharidrā, Berberis aristata (standard, by commentators); kāsīsa = green vitriol (standard); kampillaka = Mallotus philippensis (standard); saugandhika = gandhaka, sulphur (probable; the word can also mean a fragrant water lily); sarjarasa = resin of Vateria indica (probable).
lines_deva: कुष्ठामृतासङ्गकटङ्कटेरीकासीसकम्पिल्लकमुस्तलोध्राः
सौगन्धिकं सर्जरसो विडङ्गं मनःशिलाले करवीरकत्वक्
lines_iast: kuṣṭhāmṛtāsaṅgakaṭaṅkaṭerīkāsīsakampillakamustalodhrāḥ
saugandhikaṃ sarjaraso viḍaṅgaṃ manaḥśilāle karavīrakatvak

words.gloss: of one whose limbs are oiled

hindi: तैल लगे अंगों वाले व्यक्ति पर अवचूर्णन के लिए ये बनाए हुए चूर्ण डाले; इस प्रकार कण्डू सहित दद्रु, किटिभ, पामा और विचर्चिका भी शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: These prepared powders should be applied for dusting (avacūrṇana) to one whose limbs are anointed with oil; thus dadru with itching, kiṭibha, pāmā and vicarcikā also come to subsidence.
notes: dadyāt literally 'should give'. eti is singular with several subjects. vicarcikā = an eczema (probable); dadru, kiṭibha, pāmā: see unit 7 notes.
lines_deva: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य कृतानि चूर्णान्येतानि दद्यादवचूर्णनार्थम्
दद्रूः सकण्डूः किटिभानि पामा विचर्चिका चैव तथैति शान्तिम्
lines_iast: tailāktagātrasya kṛtāni cūrṇānyetāni dadyādavacūrṇanārtham
dadrūḥ sakaṇḍūḥ kiṭibhāni pāmā vicarcikā caiva tathaiti śāntim

hindi: मनःशिला और आल, मरिच, तैल और अर्क का दूध — यह कुष्ठ को हरने वाला प्रदेह है; तुत्थ, विडङ्ग, मरिच, कुष्ठ और लोध्र, मनःशिला सहित, भी वैसा ही होगा।
english: Manaḥśilā and āla, marica, oil and the latex (payas) of arka are a plaster that removes kuṣṭha; tuttha, viḍaṅga, marica, kuṣṭha and lodhra, with manaḥśilā, would likewise be so.
notes: ārkaṃ payaḥ: the milky latex of arka, Calotropis procera/gigantea (standard). tuttha = copper sulphate (standard). marica = black pepper, Piper nigrum (standard).
lines_deva: मनःशिलाले मरिचानि तैलमार्कं पयः कुष्ठहरः प्रदेहः
तुत्थं विडङ्गं मरिचानि कुष्ठं लोध्रं च तद्वत् समनःशिलं स्यात्
lines_iast: manaḥśilāle maricāni tailamārkaṃ payaḥ kuṣṭhaharaḥ pradehaḥ
tutthaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ maricāni kuṣṭhaṃ lodhraṃ ca tadvat samanaḥśilaṃ syāt

hindi: प्रपुनाड के बीजों सहित रसाञ्जन, कपित्थ के रस से युक्त, लेप है; और कुष्ठ सहित करञ्ज-बीज और एडगज, गोमूत्र में पिसे हुए, उत्तम प्रदेह है।
english: Rasāñjana with prapunāḍa seeds, mixed with the juice of kapittha, is a paste (lepa); and karañja seed and eḍagaja with kuṣṭha, ground in cow's urine, is an excellent plaster (pradeha).
notes: prapunāḍa is the usual prapunnāḍa (= eḍagaja); the short form with one n is required by the metre (upendravajrā), so it is not flagged. Identifications: rasāñjana = extract of dāruharidrā (standard); prapunnāḍa = Cassia tora (standard); kapittha = Feronia limonia (standard).
lines_deva: रसाञ्जनं सप्रपुनाडबीजं युक्तं कपित्थस्य रसेन लेपः
करञ्जबीजैडगजं सकुष्ठं गोमूत्रपिष्टं च परः प्रदेहः
lines_iast: rasāñjanaṃ saprapunāḍabījaṃ yuktaṃ kapitthasya rasena lepaḥ
karañjabījaiḍagajaṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ gomūtrapiṣṭaṃ ca paraḥ pradehaḥ

hindi: दोनों हरिद्रा, कुटज का बीज, करञ्ज का बीज, सुमना के प्रवाल और मध्य भाग सहित हयमारक की छाल — इनका तिलक्षार से युक्त लेप बनाए।
english: One should make a paste (lepa) of both haridrās, the seed of kuṭaja, karañja seed, the young shoots of sumanas and the bark of hayamāraka with its middle part, mixed with sesame alkali (tila-kṣāra).
notes: samadhyām 'with the middle (part)' is unclear: the inner part of the bark or the pith (medium). hayamāraka 'horse-killer' = karavīra, Nerium indicum (standard). kuṭaja seed = indrayava (standard). tilakṣāra = alkali made from burnt sesame plants (standard).
lines_deva: उभे हरिद्रे कुटजस्य बीजं करञ्जबीजं सुमनःप्रवालान्
त्वचं समध्यां हयमारकस्य लेपं तिलक्षारयुतं विदध्यात्
lines_iast: ubhe haridre kuṭajasya bījaṃ karañjabījaṃ sumanaḥpravālān
tvacaṃ samadhyāṃ hayamārakasya lepaṃ tilakṣārayutaṃ vidadhyāt

hindi: मनःशिला, कुष्ठ सहित कुटज की छाल, लोमश और एडगज सहित करञ्ज, और भूर्ज की ग्रन्थि, करवीर-मूल — इनके चूर्ण तुषोदक से सिद्ध करने चाहिए,
english: Manaḥśilā, the bark of kuṭaja with kuṣṭha, karañja with lomaśa and eḍagaja, the knot of bhūrja, and the root of karavīra: these powders are to be prepared with tuṣodaka,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 16. sakuṣṭhāt agrees in the ablative with kuṭajāt; read 'bark from kuṭaja, together with kuṣṭha'. tuṣodaka = a sour fermented liquid made from husked grain such as barley (standard). lomaśa: see unit 4 notes.
lines_deva: मनःशिला त्वक् कुटजात् सकुष्ठात् सलोमशः सैडगजः करञ्जः
ग्रन्थिश्च भौर्जः करवीरमूलं चूर्णानि साध्यानि तुषोदकेन
lines_iast: manaḥśilā tvak kuṭajāt sakuṣṭhāt salomaśaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjaḥ
granthiśca bhaurjaḥ karavīramūlaṃ cūrṇāni sādhyāni tuṣodakena

words.gloss: with the liquid of burnt palāśa

words.gram: n. nom. pl. tat-puruṣa, ppp. ud-√hṛ

hindi: और एक आढक मात्रा वाले पलाश-निर्दाह-रस से भी, एक-एक कर्ष लेकर; इस दर्वीप्रलेप लेप को कुष्ठ के नाश के लिए उत्तम कहते हैं।
english: and also with the liquid of burnt palāśa measuring one āḍhaka, taken a karṣa each; this paste, smearing the ladle (darvī-pralepa), they declare supreme for destroying kuṣṭha.
notes: Continues unit 15: the powders, one karṣa of each, are cooked in tuṣodaka and an āḍhaka of palāśa liquid until the paste coats the ladle. palāśanirdāharasa: the liquid from burnt palāśa (Butea monosperma, standard), taken by commentators as alkaline water from its ash (probable). karṣa and āḍhaka are measures (a karṣa is commonly reckoned about 12 g; an āḍhaka about 3 kg or litres; standard reckonings vary).
lines_deva: पलाशनिर्दाहरसेन चापि कर्षोद्धृतान्याढकसंमितेन
दर्वीप्रलेपं प्रवदन्ति लेपमेतं परं कुष्ठनिसूदनाय
lines_iast: palāśanirdāharasena cāpi karṣoddhṛtānyāḍhakasaṃmitena
darvīpralepaṃ pravadanti lepametaṃ paraṃ kuṣṭhanisūdanāya

hindi: चतुरङ्गुल के पत्तों को, फिर काकमाची के पत्तों को, तक्र के साथ पीसकर, तथा अश्वहन के पत्तों से भी, तैल लगे अंगों वाले मनुष्य के कुष्ठों का उद्वर्तन करे।
english: Having ground the leaves of caturaṅgula with buttermilk, then the leaves of kākamācī, and with the leaves of aśvahana, one should rub (udvartana) the kuṣṭhas of a man whose limbs are anointed with oil.
notes: takreṇa may go with both sets of leaves. Identifications: caturaṅgula = āragvadha, Cassia fistula (standard, by commentators); kākamācī = Solanum nigrum (standard); aśvahana 'horse-killer' = karavīra, Nerium indicum (standard). The single printed token kuṣṭhānyudvartayedaśvahanacchadaiśca is split into its four words.
lines_deva: पर्णानि पिष्ट्वा चतुरङ्गुलस्य तक्रेण पर्णान्यथ काकमाच्याः
तैलाक्तगात्रस्य नरस्य कुष्ठान्युद्वर्तयेदश्वहनच्छदैश्च
lines_iast: parṇāni piṣṭvā caturaṅgulasya takreṇa parṇānyatha kākamācyāḥ
tailāktagātrasya narasya kuṣṭhānyudvartayedaśvahanacchadaiśca

words.gloss: suradāru, rāsnā, māṣa, atasī and oil-seeds

hindi: कोल, कुलत्थ, सुरदारु, रास्ना, माष, अतसी और तैलफल, कुष्ठ, वचा, शताह्वा, यव-चूर्ण और अम्ल — उष्ण रूप में ये वात-रोगियों के लिए प्रदेह हैं।
english: Kola, kulattha, suradāru, rāsnā, māṣa, atasī and oil-seeds, kuṣṭha, vacā, śatāhvā, barley flour and amla (sour): warm, these are a plaster for those suffering from Vāta diseases.

text_flags.why: The line has 21 syllables; with tailaphalāni pāda b of line a (māṣātasītailaphalāni kuṣṭham) has 11 syllables and fits indravajrā exactly; 'tailapha' is not a word. The Devanagari (तैलफानि) has the same omission of ला. Typing error.

notes: tailaphala = oil-yielding seeds such as tila and sarṣapa (probable). amla is taken as a sour liquid such as kāñjika (probable). Identifications: kola = Ziziphus jujuba (standard); kulattha = Dolichos biflorus (standard); rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (disputed; also Alpinia galanga); māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard); atasī = linseed, Linum usitatissimum (standard); śatāhvā = dill, Anethum sowa (standard).
lines_deva: कोलं कुलत्थाः सुरदारुरास्नामाषातसीतैलफानि कुष्ठम्
वचा शताह्वा यवचूर्णमम्लमुष्णानि वातामयिनां प्रदेहः
lines_iast: kolaṃ kulatthāḥ suradārurāsnāmāṣātasītailaphāni kuṣṭham
vacā śatāhvā yavacūrṇamamlamuṣṇāni vātāmayināṃ pradehaḥ

words.gloss: with vesavāra of marsh fish and flesh

hindi: आनूप मत्स्य और मांस के उष्ण वेसवारों से प्रदेह वात को दूर करने वाला होता है; दशमूल मिले चार स्नेहों से और गन्ध-औषधों से प्रदेह वात को नष्ट करने वाला होता है।
english: A plaster with warm vesavāra of marsh (ānūpa) fish and flesh would remove Vāta (pavana); a plaster with the four fats (sneha) mixed with daśamūla, and with fragrant drugs, destroys Vāta (anila).
notes: vesavāra = boneless meat minced, steamed and spiced (standard). ānūpa is read as qualifying both fish and flesh. The four snehas = ghee, oil, muscle-fat (vasā) and marrow (majjā) (standard). daśamūla = the group of ten roots (standard). In the Hindi both pavana and anila are rendered वात per the glossary.
lines_deva: आनूपमत्स्यामिषवेसवारैरुष्णैः प्रदेहः पवनापहः स्यात्
स्नेहैश्चतुर्भिर्दशमूलमिश्रैर्गन्धौषधैश्चानिलहः प्रदेहः
lines_iast: ānūpamatsyāmiṣavesavārairuṣṇaiḥ pradehaḥ pavanāpahaḥ syāt
snehaiścaturbhirdaśamūlamiśrairgandhauṣadhaiścānilahaḥ pradehaḥ

hindi: तक्र से युक्त, क्षार सहित उष्ण यव-चूर्ण जठर की पीड़ा को नष्ट करे; वचा सहित कुष्ठ और शताह्वा, तथा यवों का चूर्ण, तैल और अम्ल सहित, वात में बताते हैं।
english: Warm barley flour mixed with buttermilk, with alkali (kṣāra), would destroy pain in the abdomen; kuṣṭha and śatāhvā with vacā, and the flour of barley, with oil and amla (sour), they recommend in Vāta.
notes: savacām agrees with śatāhvām. yavānām is gen. pl. of yava (barley); reading it as yavānī (ajowan) would need a different form. uśanti (√vaś 'wish') is used in the sense 'recommend'. The application form (plaster) is implied by context.
lines_deva: तक्रेण युक्तं यवचूर्णमुष्णं सक्षारमर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्
कुष्ठं शताह्वां सवचां यवानां चूर्णं सतैलाम्लमुशन्ति वाते
lines_iast: takreṇa yuktaṃ yavacūrṇamuṣṇaṃ sakṣāramartiṃ jaṭhare nihanyāt
kuṣṭhaṃ śatāhvāṃ savacāṃ yavānāṃ cūrṇaṃ satailāmlamuśanti vāte

hindi: दोनों शताह्वा, मधुक, मधूक, बला, प्रियाल और कशेरुक, घृत, विदारी और सितोपला — इनका प्रदेह रक्त सहित वात में करे।
english: In Vāta (pavana) with blood (rakta), one should make a plaster of both śatāhvās, madhuka, madhūka, balā, priyāla and kaśeruka, ghee, vidārī and sugar candy (sitopalā).
notes: pavane sarakte = Vāta combined with rakta, i.e. vātarakta, often equated with gout (probable). The two śatāhvās are taken as śatāhvā and miśreyā (disputed). Identifications: madhuka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra (standard); madhūka = Madhuca indica (standard); balā = Sida cordifolia (standard); priyāla = Buchanania lanzan (standard); kaśeruka = Scirpus grossus (probable); vidārī = Pueraria tuberosa (probable).
lines_deva: उभे शताह्वे मधुकं मधूकं बलां प्रियालं च कशेरुकं च
घृतं विदारीं च सितोपलां च कुर्यात् प्रदेहं पवने सरक्ते
lines_iast: ubhe śatāhve madhukaṃ madhūkaṃ balāṃ priyālaṃ ca kaśerukaṃ ca
ghṛtaṃ vidārīṃ ca sitopalāṃ ca kuryāt pradehaṃ pavane sarakte

hindi: रास्ना, गुडूची, मधुक, दोनों बला, जीवक और ऋषभक सहित, और दूध; तथा सिद्ध किया हुआ, मधुशेष से युक्त घृत — यह प्रदेह रक्त और वात की पीड़ा को दूर करे।
english: Rāsnā, guḍūcī, madhuka, the two balās, with jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka, and milk; and ghee, cooked (siddha) and mixed with beeswax (madhuśeṣa): as a plaster it would dispel the pain of rakta and Vāta (anila).
notes: siddham probably means the ghee is cooked with the listed drugs and milk (commentators), but the text only says 'cooked'. sarṣabhakam = sa + ṛṣabhakam. The two balās = balā and atibalā (probable). jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka are drugs of the aṣṭavarga group, unidentified with certainty (disputed). madhuśeṣa 'remainder of honey' = beeswax (standard).
lines_deva: रास्ना गुडूची मधुकं बले द्वे सजीवकं सर्षभकं पयश्च
घृतं च सिद्धं मधुशेषयुक्तं रक्तानिलार्तिं प्रणुदेत् प्रदेहः
lines_iast: rāsnā guḍūcī madhukaṃ bale dve sajīvakaṃ sarṣabhakaṃ payaśca
ghṛtaṃ ca siddhaṃ madhuśeṣayuktaṃ raktānilārtiṃ praṇudet pradehaḥ

hindi: रक्त सहित वात में घृत सहित गोधूम-चूर्ण और बकरी का दूध प्रदेह है; चन्दन और कुष्ठ से युक्त, घृत सहित नत और उत्पल शिरोरुजा में प्रदेह है।
english: In Vāta with rakta, wheat flour and goat's milk with ghee is a plaster; nata and utpala, mixed with candana and kuṣṭha, with ghee, is a plaster in headache.
notes: Identifications: nata = tagara, Valeriana wallichii (standard); utpala = blue water lily, Nymphaea stellata (standard); candana = sandalwood, Santalum album (standard).
lines_deva: वाते सरक्ते सघृतं प्रदेहो गोधूमचूर्णं छगलीपयश्च
नतोत्पलं चन्दनकुष्ठयुक्तं शिरोरुजायां सघृतं प्रदेहः
lines_iast: vāte sarakte saghṛtaṃ pradeho godhūmacūrṇaṃ chagalīpayaśca
natotpalaṃ candanakuṣṭhayuktaṃ śirorujāyāṃ saghṛtaṃ pradehaḥ

words.gloss: with loha, erakā, padmaka and coraka

hindi: प्रपौण्डरीक, सुरदारु, कुष्ठ, यष्ट्याह्व, एला, कमल और उत्पल, तथा लोह, एरका, पद्मक और चोरक के साथ — घृत सहित प्रदेह शिरोरुजा में है।
english: Prapauṇḍarīka, suradāru, kuṣṭha, yaṣṭyāhva, elā, kamala and utpala, and with loha, erakā, padmaka and coraka: a plaster with ghee in headache.
notes: loha in this list of plant drugs is taken by commentators as aguru (probable), not metal; the word is kept as loha. Identifications: prapauṇḍarīka = a lotus-like drug (disputed); yaṣṭyāhva = yaṣṭimadhu, liquorice (standard); kamala = Nelumbo nucifera (standard); erakā = Typha elephantina (probable); padmaka = Prunus cerasoides (standard); coraka = Angelica glauca (probable).
lines_deva: प्रपौण्डरीकं सुरदारु कुष्ठं यष्ट्याह्वमेला कमलोत्पले च
शिरोरुजायां सघृतः प्रदेहो लोहैरकापद्मकचोरकैश्च
lines_iast: prapauṇḍarīkaṃ suradāru kuṣṭhaṃ yaṣṭyāhvamelā kamalotpale ca
śirorujāyāṃ saghṛtaḥ pradeho lohairakāpadmakacorakaiśca

hindi: रास्ना, दोनों हरिद्रा, नलद, दोनों शताह्वा, देवदारु, सितोपला और जीवन्ती-मूल — घृत और तैल सहित, कुछ गरम आलेपन पार्श्वरुजा में है।
english: Rāsnā, the two haridrās, nalada, the two śatāhvās, devadāru, sitopalā and the root of jīvantī, with ghee and with oil, lukewarm, is an ointment (ālepana) in pains of the sides.
notes: dve (f. du.) is read with śatāhve (f. du.) before it; it cannot agree with devadārūṇi (n. pl.), though it opens the second quarter of the verse. Some read 'dve devadārūṇi' as two kinds of devadāru; the number mismatch makes this less likely. jīvanti- is the compound form of jīvantī. Identifications: nalada = jaṭāmāṃsī, Nardostachys jatamansi (standard); jīvantī = Leptadenia reticulata (probable).
lines_deva: रास्ना हरिद्रे नलदं शताह्वे द्वे देवदारूणि सितोपला च
जीवन्तिमूलं सघृतं सतैलमालेपनं पार्श्वरुजासु कोष्णम्
lines_iast: rāsnā haridre naladaṃ śatāhve dve devadārūṇi sitopalā ca
jīvantimūlaṃ saghṛtaṃ satailamālepanaṃ pārśvarujāsu koṣṇam

words.gloss: śaivāla, padma, utpala, vetra, tuṅga and prapauṇḍarīka

hindi: शैवाल, पद्म, उत्पल, वेत्र, तुङ्ग, प्रपौण्डरीक, अमृणाल और लोध्र, प्रियङ्गु, कालेयक और चन्दन — घृत सहित यह प्रदेह निर्वापण करने वाला होता है।
english: Śaivāla, padma, utpala, vetra, tuṅga, prapauṇḍarīka, amṛṇāla and lodhra, priyaṅgu, kāleyaka and candana: with ghee, the plaster would be cooling (nirvāpaṇa).
notes: nirvāpaṇa 'extinguishing', i.e. cooling, relieving burning (standard sense). Identifications: śaivāla = an aquatic weed, Vallisneria spiralis (probable); padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (standard); vetra = Calamus rotang (standard); tuṅga = punnāga, Calophyllum inophyllum (probable); amṛṇāla = uśīra, vetiver, Vetiveria zizanioides (standard, by commentators); priyaṅgu = Callicarpa macrophylla (standard); kāleyaka = a yellow fragrant wood (disputed).
lines_deva: शैवालपद्मोत्पलवेत्रतुङ्गप्रपौण्डरीकाण्यमृणाललोध्रम्
प्रियङ्गुकालेयकचन्दनानि निर्वापणः स्यात् सघृतः प्रदेहः
lines_iast: śaivālapadmotpalavetratuṅgaprapauṇḍarīkāṇyamṛṇālalodhram
priyaṅgukāleyakacandanāni nirvāpaṇaḥ syāt saghṛtaḥ pradehaḥ

hindi: सिता, लता, वेतस और पद्मक, यष्ट्याह्व, ऐन्द्री, नलिन, दूर्वा, यवास-मूल और कुश तथा काश का मूल, जल और एरका — यह निर्वापण करने वाला होता है।
english: Sitā, latā, vetasa and padmaka, yaṣṭyāhva, aindrī, nalinas, dūrvā, the root of yavāsa and of kuśa and kāśa, jala and erakā: this would be cooling (nirvāpaṇa).
notes: sitālatā can also be one name ('white creeper', e.g. white dūrvā); the split sitā (sugar) + latā (priyaṅgu or mañjiṣṭhā) is disputed. jala may be water or the drug hrībera (Pavonia odorata) (probable for the drug sense); kept as jala. nirvāpaṇaḥ (m.) implies pradehaḥ from unit 26; 'this' in the translation stands for it. Identifications: vetasa = Salix caprea or Calamus (disputed); aindrī = indravāruṇī or brāhmī (disputed); dūrvā = Cynodon dactylon (standard); yavāsa = Alhagi camelorum (probable); kuśa = Desmostachya bipinnata (standard); kāśa = Saccharum spontaneum (standard).
lines_deva: सितालतावेतसपद्मकानि यष्ट्याह्वमैन्द्री नलिनानि दूर्वा
यवासमूलं कुशकाशयोश्च निर्वापणः स्याज्जलमेरका च
lines_iast: sitālatāvetasapadmakāni yaṣṭyāhvamaindrī nalināni dūrvā
yavāsamūlaṃ kuśakāśayośca nirvāpaṇaḥ syājjalamerakā ca

hindi: शैलेय, कुष्ठ सहित एला और अगुरु, चण्डा, नत, त्वक्, सुरदारु और रास्ना — यह प्रदेह शीत को शीघ्र नष्ट करे; और सिन्धुवार सहित शिरीष विष को।
english: Śaileya, elā and aguru with kuṣṭha, caṇḍā, nata, tvak, suradāru and rāsnā: as a plaster it would quickly destroy cold; and śirīṣa with sindhuvāra, poison.
notes: śītam: the sensation or condition of cold. In line b nihanyāt and pradehaḥ are understood again with śirīṣa. tvak in drug lists = cinnamon bark, Cinnamomum zeylanicum (standard). Identifications: śaileya = a lichen, Parmelia perlata (probable); aguru = Aquilaria agallocha (standard); sindhuvāra = Vitex negundo (standard); caṇḍā: see unit 8.
lines_deva: शैलेयमेलागुरुणी सकुष्ठे चण्डा नतं त्वक् सुरदारु रास्ना
शीतं निहन्यादचिरात् प्रदेहो विषं शिरीषस्तु ससिन्धुवारः
lines_iast: śaileyamelāguruṇī sakuṣṭhe caṇḍā nataṃ tvak suradāru rāsnā
śītaṃ nihanyādacirāt pradeho viṣaṃ śirīṣastu sasindhuvāraḥ

words.gloss: with śirīṣa, lāmajjaka, hema and lodhra
removing skin disorders and profuse sweat
patra, ambu, lodhra, abhaya and candana

hindi: शिरीष, लामज्जक, हेम और लोध्र से प्रघर्ष त्वग्दोष और संस्वेद को हरने वाला है; पत्र, अम्बु, लोध्र, अभय और चन्दन — यह प्रदेह शरीर की दुर्गन्ध को हरने वाला है।
english: Rubbing (pragharṣa) with śirīṣa, lāmajjaka, hema and lodhra removes skin disorders (tvag-doṣa) and profuse sweating (saṃsveda); patra, ambu, lodhra, abhaya and candana are a plaster that removes bad odour of the body.
notes: abhaya in the compound may stand for abhayā (harītakī, Terminalia chebula) or for uśīra (some commentators) (disputed). Identifications: lāmajjaka = a fragrant grass related to uśīra (probable); hema = nāgakeśara (disputed); patra = tejapatra, Cinnamomum tamala (probable); ambu = hrībera, Pavonia odorata (probable).
lines_deva: शिरीषलामज्जकहेमलोध्रैस्त्वग्दोषसंस्वेदहरः प्रघर्षः
पत्राम्बुलोध्राभयचन्दनानि शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः प्रदेहः
lines_iast: śirīṣalāmajjakahemalodhraistvagdoṣasaṃsvedaharaḥ pragharṣaḥ
patrāmbulodhrābhayacandanāni śarīradaurgandhyaharaḥ pradehaḥ

words.gloss: revered by siddhas and great sages

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक है — यहाँ आरग्वधीय में सिद्धों और महर्षियों द्वारा पूज्य अत्रि-पुत्र ने जगत् के हित के लिए विविध रोगों को नष्ट करने वाले बत्तीस अत्यन्त सिद्ध चूर्ण-प्रदेह कहे।
english: Here is a verse: here, in the Āragvadhīya, the son of Atri, revered by siddhas and great sages, taught, for the welfare of the world, thirty-two most proven powder-plasters (cūrṇa-pradeha) that destroy various diseases.
notes: Line a 'tatra ślokaḥ' (singular: one verse follows) is the lead-in of the closing summary; it is kept as a line of this unit as the edition groups it. atrijaḥ 'born of Atri' is an epithet (it refers to Ātreya); the translation keeps the epithet. siddha-maharṣi- may also be read 'perfected great sages' (karmadhāraya). The thirty-two are the formulations of this chapter as counted by the text.
lines_deva: तत्र श्लोकः ---
इहात्रिजः सिद्धतमानुवाच द्वात्रिंशतं सिद्धमहर्षिपूज्यः
चूर्णप्रदेहान् विविधामयघ्नानारग्वधीये जगतो हितार्थम्
lines_iast: tatra ślokaḥ ---
ihātrijaḥ siddhatamānuvāca dvātriṃśataṃ siddhamaharṣipūjyaḥ
cūrṇapradehān vividhāmayaghnānāragvadhīye jagato hitārtham

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में आरग्वधीय नामक तीसरा अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna) of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the third chapter, named Āragvadhīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless. Ślokasthāna is another name of the Sūtrasthāna (the chapter 1 colophon reads sūtrasthāne); not flagged. ślokasthāne āragvadhīyo is printed without sandhi, as often in colophons.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने आरग्वधीयो नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne āragvadhīyo nāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ
